title: fix(metadata-protocol,rest,runtime): beside a disabled package, the bare read, /layers and /published serve the one enabled holder of a doc, view or other type the registry does not read by package
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbNTugWasvhTMrtCZiFGrZYK)_

Fixes #34041

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：同名元数据由“一个启用包 + 一个停用包”同时发布时，不带包名的读取、`/layers` 和 `/published` 现在都返回启用包的条目。覆盖 doc、view、translation、hook 等所有“注册表不按包读取”的类型（object、action、package 除外）。
- 为什么改：ADR-0150 D3 规定停用的包不持有名字。原来这些类型按名字取第一层（元数据服务里最后注册的副本，或注册表的第一个组合项），如果取到的是停用包的，普通读取返回 404，`/layers` 甚至把停用包的正文当作 effective 返回。
- 风险与回滚：只在“名字的持有者里有停用包、且只剩一个启用持有者”时改变答案。两个启用持有者照旧 409，全部停用照旧 404，action 与保存门不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts`（`servedHolderAddressOf` 去掉 readsByPackage 门槛，新增 `SERVED_HOLDER_JUDGED_ELSEWHERE`）；`packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts` 与 `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` 中 `/published` 的 mixed-owner 分支（同一条件，两处孪生）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-artifact-door.test.ts`，预期 23 passed，`[#34041]` 组在两种注册顺序下全部为绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

ADR-0150 D3 says a disabled package holds no name. For a type the registry reads by package, the read naming no package already took the served holder's address when a disabled package also holds the name (`servedHolderAddressOf`, #32183). Every other type read the layer it finds by name alone. That layer is the metadata service's copy, which belongs to the package registered last, or else the registry's first composite. Either one could be the disabled holder's. The face then withheld it, so the plain read answered 404, and `/layers` served the disabled body as `effective`.

- **`servedHolderAddressOf`** (`protocol-meta-item-face.ts`) no longer requires `readsByPackage(type)`. It re-addresses every type except those `SERVED_HOLDER_JUDGED_ELSEWHERE` names: `object` (one owner, refused with its disabled package), `action` (its bare judge `judgeBareActionRead` already serves the one enabled holder; measured unchanged) and `package`. Read at the served holder's address, the read is that holder's exact read, which never answers another package's service copy (`serviceCopyOfAnotherPackage`, #34241). Its callers in `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` and `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` needed no edit.
- **The `/published` door twins** (`rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts`, `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`): the mixed-owner arm's `readsByPackage(type) === true` conjunct becomes "type is not `action`" (`object` and `package` are excluded there already). Without this, once the plain read served the enabled holder, the snapshot exit served the metadata service's `getPublished` copy, which is the disabled holder's body (measured: 200 `beta doc` on both transports). The claim amendment (comment 6908475841) widened the file surface to these two files.

## FROM → TO

One enabled holder (alpha) and one disabled holder (beta) of a name, for each of `doc`, `view`, `translation`, `field`, `seed`, `datasource`, `external_catalog`, `object_extension`, `hook`, `job`, `sharing_rule`, `queue` and `assignment_rule`:

| Door | FROM (main) | TO |
|---|---|---|
| bare `GET /meta/TYPE/NAME`, when the layer read by name is beta's (the service copy with beta registered last, or the registry's first composite with beta registered first and no copy) | 404 | 200, alpha's item |
| bare `/layers`, same states | 200, `effective` = beta's body | 200, `effective` = alpha's item |
| bare `/published` (doc, composed rig, beta registered last) | 404 | 200, alpha's doc |
| the same doors when the layer read by name is already alpha's | 200, alpha | unchanged |
| two enabled holders of a doc | 409 naming both | unchanged |
| both holders disabled | 404 | unchanged |
| `action`, `object`, `package`; a name no disabled package holds | as on main | unchanged |
| bare `PUT /meta/doc/NAME` beside a disabled holder | 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` (sealed) | unchanged |

Nothing served becomes refused, so `Clause-②: no` holds as claimed. No authorable key, value or type moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds too.

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`, a new top-level describe `[#34041]` beside the #34040 type enumeration. It holds an enumeration pin (every type the registry does not read by package is pinned, one-holder, or judged elsewhere). Per type, in both orders, with beta disabled, the plain read and `/layers` serve alpha in each of three service states (no copy, alpha's copy, beta's copy), and with both disabled there is no item. CONTROLs: a doc with two enabled holders is refused 409 naming both, before and after a disable and re-enable; an action is unchanged; a view with no disabled holder reads as before.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-artifact-door.test.ts`, a new `describe.each` `[#34041]` on the composed artifact rig (the `MetadataPlugin` artifact door plus `AppPlugin`), on both transports and in both orders. With beta disabled, the plain read, `/layers` (code and effective) and `/published` serve `alpha doc` and never `# beta`. CONTROL: with both disabled, every door answers 404; with both re-enabled, every door refuses 409 naming both.

<details><summary>Reverse verification against origin/main 01598d936f (before the fix)</summary>

- objectql describe: `Tests 28 failed | 4 passed`. Example, view with beta registered last and the service keeping beta's copy: Received `[undefined, "beta view"]`, Expected `["alpha view", "alpha view"]`.
- Composed rig: the dispatcher plain read Received `404 undefined`, Expected `200 "alpha doc"`.
- With only the face fix (before the door half): the rig's only red rows were `dispatcher doc/shared_doc/published` and `rest doc/shared_doc/published`, Received `200 "beta doc"`.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (ablation-replace; restore blob equals HEAD; git diff HEAD empty; tree clean)</summary>

- Leg 1, the `readsByPackage` gate put back in `servedHolderAddressOf` (metadata-protocol resolves through `dist/` in both suites, so it was rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 2 built files, and after restore and rebuild `--absent` found it in none of 24). objectql: `Tests 28 failed | 352 passed (380)`, e.g. Received `undefined, "beta view"`. Rig: `1 failed | 22 passed`, with all six door rows red. The first attempt at this leg was a no-op: the build folded its string marker away, preflight reported it ABSENT, and nothing ran. It was redone with a marker that reaches `dist/`.
- Leg 2, the gate put back in the RestServer `/published` arm (runtime aliases `@objectstack/rest` to `src`): rig `1 failed | 22 passed`, the only red row `rest doc/shared_doc/published`, Received `"beta doc"`.
- Leg 3, the gate put back in the dispatcher `/published` arm: rig `1 failed | 22 passed`, the only red row `dispatcher doc/shared_doc/published`, Received `"beta doc"`.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- `servedPackagelessSaveAddress` (`protocol-save.ts`, not edited) asks the same judgment. For a doc beside a disabled holder, the bare save is refused 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` (a sealed managed package) both before and after this change, in both orders, so the save is unchanged. This was measured with a scratch probe on the composed rig.
- The light harness also shows the second state on main: with no service copy and the disabled holder registered first, the registry's first composite was the disabled body. The fix covers that state too, and the pin enumerates it.

## Verification

- **Head 662c7c973e** (origin/main 35c9a305f0 merged in, which brings #33995's edits to the same face and door files; merge-tree was clean and the merge had no conflict): rebuilt; `typecheck` exit 0 for metadata-protocol, objectql, rest and runtime. **NOT MEASURED at this head**: the suites, the two pin files and the derived gates. Reason: a maintainer order to hand off now stopped that run, so the readings below are from the previous head. The next seat (or CI) re-runs them.
